trends.name: Embedding outliers + spatial
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around spatial, visual, video, with representative work on SegPVSG: Panoptic Video Scene Graph Generation via Temporal Focusing and Generative Augmentation.
trends.coreQuestion: How can spatial approaches be used for visual?
representativeSentences: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to parse an image into a structured graph of objects and their predicates, enabling explicit relational reasoning for visual understanding.
Geospatial understanding is a critical yet underexplored dimension in the development of machine learning systems for tasks such as image geolocation and spatial reasoning.
Collectively, these contributions offer a universal and effective suite for joint spatial-temporal video understanding, setting a new standard in multimodal intelligence.

trends.name: Cluster 01: optimization / learning + diffusion
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around diffusion, sampling, gradient, with representative work on Optimal Stopping in Latent Diffusion Models.
trends.coreQuestion: How can diffusion approaches be used for sampling?
representativeSentences: There has been a proliferation of sampling algorithms based on Wasserstein gradient flows (WGF) and forward-only diffusion processes (FODP), often accompanied by theoretical guarantees of exponentially fast convergence to the target distribution.

Although these dynamics require sampling from a non-trivial initialization distribution, we show both theoretically and empirically that the cost of this initialization diminishes for sufficiently short diffusion times.
We establish rigorous theoretical bounds on the loss incurred when sampling from the CGMMD sampler, and prove convergence of the estimated distribution to the true conditional distribution.

trends.name: Cluster 03: decoding / diffusion + decoding
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around decoding, speculative decoding, speculative, with representative work on Select to Think: Unlocking SLM Potential with Local Sufficiency.
trends.coreQuestion: How can decoding approaches be used for speculative decoding?
representativeSentences: Speculative decoding has emerged as a widely adopted paradigm for accelerating large language model inference, where a lightweight draft model rapidly generates candidate tokens that are then verified in parallel by a larger target model.

Diffusion Language Models (DLLMs) offer parallel decoding by recovering multiple masked tokens per step; however, in practice they often fail to translate this parallelism into speed gains over optimized AR engines (e.g., vLLM).
Speculative decoding (SD) is a well-established technique for serving fixed LLMs that reduces latency by drafting tokens and verifying them in parallel.

trends.coreQuestion: How can regret approaches be used for online?

We then propose SERMiSC, a novel algorithm that achieves the optimal trade-off by matching this lower bound while maintaining a near-constant $\tilde{O}(1)$ safety risk.
Both algorithms achieve improved theoretical guarantees using machine-learned predictions of an optimal solution to the dual linear program.

trends.coreQuestion: How can treatment approaches be used for survival?
representativeSentences: For fully nonparametric regression with functional covariates, we establish a lower bound on the prediction error, and further discuss the fundamental obstacles inherent to this problem and their connections to existing state-of-the-art methods in the literature.
In this work, we study the theoretical performance of DNN-based estimators for regression problems with functional covariates.

Regression with functional covariates poses fundamental challenges due to the infinite-dimensional nature of functional data, and its theoretical properties have been studied under specialized frameworks in classical nonparametric statistics.

trends.name: Cluster 05: graph / learning + graph

trends.coreQuestion: How can graph approaches be used for graphs?
representativeSentences: The DeepWalk algorithm has been widely used for learning node embeddings in graphs.

We frame this problem as a self-supervised learning task and present several methods to generate graph alignment datasets using synthetic random graphs and real-world graph datasets from multiple domains.

trends.name: Cluster 06: adversarial / attacks + backdoor
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around backdoor, attacks, attack, with representative work on TimeGuard: Channel-wise Pool Training for Backdoor Defense in Time Series Forecasting.
trends.coreQuestion: How can backdoor approaches be used for attacks?
representativeSentences: Empirically, BYORn consistently improves robustness to backdoor attacks while preserving clean-task performance, establishing a new trade-off frontier between generalization and attack success rate.
Recent work has shown that this paradigm is highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and that existing defenses are ineffective in open-ended generation settings.
Time Series Forecasting (TSF) plays a critical role across many domains, yet it is vulnerable to backdoor attacks.

trends.name: Cluster 07: neural / learning + neural
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around neural, pdes, pinns, with representative work on Origo: Physically Interpretable Multi-Physics PDE Pre-training through Neural Operator Splitting.
trends.coreQuestion: How can neural approaches be used for pdes?
representativeSentences: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often train slowly or fail to converge on challenging partial differential equations (PDEs), a behavior recently linked to severely ill-conditioned loss landscapes inherited from the underlying differential operator.
Here we propose the Adaptive Physics Transformer (APT), a geometry-, mesh-, and physics-agnostic neural operator that explicitly addresses these challenges.
A key innovation is Origo, which provides a neural operator bank that enables the identification of operator-level generalization patterns.

trends.name: Cluster 08: learning / policy + policy
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around policy, reinforcement learning, policies, with representative work on Mind Your Entropy: From Maximum Entropy to Trajectory Entropy-Constrained RL.
trends.coreQuestion: How can policy approaches be used for reinforcement learning?
representativeSentences: Experiments on the D4RL benchmark demonstrate that semantically grounded value gradients provide a principled, effective foundation for training diffusion policies in offline reinforcement learning.
Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning (O2O-RL) leverages an offline, pre-trained policy to minimize costly online interactions.
Generative models have emerged as a powerful class of policies for offline reinforcement learning (RL) due to their ability to capture complex, multi-modal behaviors.

trends.name: Cluster 09: reasoning / learning + reasoning
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around reasoning, reinforcement learning, reinforcement, with representative work on EAPO: Enhancing Policy Optimization with On-Demand Expert Assistance.
trends.coreQuestion: How can reasoning approaches be used for reinforcement learning?
representativeSentences: Large language models (LLMs) have recently advanced in reasoning when optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) under verifiable rewards.
Recent success of large reasoning models (such as OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek R1) have spurred a resurgence of interest in reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR).
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can improve LLM reasoning, but learning is sample-inefficient under sparse terminal rewards.

trends.name: Cluster 13: protein / design + protein
trends.summary: This trend groups papers around protein, design, generation, with representative work on MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects.
trends.coreQuestion: How can protein approaches be used for design?
representativeSentences: Despite its importance to applications in protein design, predicting protein properties like binding affinity and thermostability from sparse experimental data remains a significant challenge.
Computational protein design typically employs a sequential workflow of structure generation followed by sequence (re)design.
Post-translational modifications (PTMs) dynamically reshape the binding landscapes of protein drug targets, yet no computational method predicts how specific PTMs alter drug binding affinity.

trends.name: Cluster 11: attention / memory + attention

trends.coreQuestion: How can attention approaches be used for memory?
representativeSentences: Linear recurrent models, such as linear attention and state space models, have become widely studied as alternatives due to their linear compute and constant memory requirements.

Experimental results show that Token Sparse Attention consistently improves accuracy–latency trade-off, achieving up to $\times$3.23 attention speedup at 128K context with less than 1\% accuracy degradation.
Furthermore, Token Sparse Attention exposes a new design point at the intersection of token selection and sparse attention.
